first_impression.reaction: I jumped to the FAQ first, like I always do. No pricing section, so I went back up. The intro is fine. It's plain, no 'best garden weddings in the world' stuff, and this line actually admits the downside: "the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather." That's enough to get me to the venue questions, which is the only part I really came for. I skimmed the styling.

journey.quote: It works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together, because the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.
journey.reaction: Good. They lead with the trade-off, not the dream. I'll give them a few more minutes.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: The gardens gave their guests a warm, romantic space to spend it in.
journey.reaction: Means nothing. Eight weddings and not one guest count, month, budget or wet weather outcome. I wanted to see what one of these actually cost and what went wrong. Right now they're mood boards with names on them.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: Eight couples and eight gardens, each described as their own story tells it.
journey.reaction: At least they're upfront that this is just their own write-ups, linked. I can check them. Doesn't prove much, but it isn't pretending to be more.

journey.section: What to plan for with your venue
journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to ask before you book, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: This is the useful bit. 'Get it in writing' is exactly what I learned the hard way last time.

journey.section: Wet weather plan and covered space
journey.quote: Who makes the call to move under cover, and by what time on the day?
journey.reaction: That's a real question nobody asked our last vendor. I'm putting this in my spreadsheet.

journey.quote: recommends sun protection whenever the UV level reaches 3 or higher, and UV cannot be seen or felt, so check the UV forecast for the location on the SunSmart app or the Bureau of Meteorology website.
journey.reaction: A number and a named source I can check. More of this, please.

journey.quote: Bring this list to your first conversation with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=garden-wedding&utm_content=primary).
journey.reaction: There's the pitch. It comes after the checklist, so it's not as bad as some, but it reads like the list exists to get me on a call. The list is for my venue visits.

journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Concrete and checkable. Quotes in AUD and inclusions in writing are things I can hold them to.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'The fee is agreed in writing' is better than nothing, but agreed how? Flat fee, percentage, or do the venues pay you? 'Plans the payments' makes me more nervous, not less. If the money goes through you, I want to know whether there's a margin on it.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance.
journey.reaction: 'Loveliest.' This is the copywriter talking. It's also a bit of a scare line to push me into the form.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out: flat fee, percentage of budget, or something else?
Do you take a commission or referral fee from venues or vendors you recommend?
Are supplier prices passed through at cost, or is there a mark-up when you handle the payments?
What does the fee include and what costs extra?
What did any of these eight real weddings actually cost, and how many guests did they have?
Did any of the featured couples have to use their wet weather plan, and how did it go?
Where can I read independent reviews of Wedded Concierge?

turn_offs_found.quote: A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional language right where I'm deciding whether to enquire. Tell me what you do, not how lovely it is.

turn_offs_found.quote: The gardens gave their guests a warm, romantic space to spend it in.
turn_offs_found.why: Fluff in the one section that was supposed to be proof. No facts I can use.

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions the fee but hides how it works, and says nothing about commissions. That's the catch I'm looking for.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the venue question lists only

cta_reaction.quote: Tell [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=garden-wedding&utm_content=closing) the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
cta_reaction.why: The checklist earned some credit and 'inclusions in writing' helps. But I won't hand over details until I know how the fee works and whether you take a cut from venues. If the page told me where to find that, I'd click. As it stands I'd go looking on the rest of the site first, and if it's not there, I'm comparing the other two planners.

top_3_changes: Closing section: replace the 'loveliest setting' line with a plain statement of the trade-off. Old: "A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance." New: "A garden has more to settle in advance than an indoor room, and more that can change on the day."

Closing CTA: invite the fee question instead of avoiding it. Old: "the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming." New: "the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming, and ask how the fee is worked out before you commit to anything."

Mid-page CTA: make the checklist about the reader's venue visits first, with the concierge second. Old: "Bring this list to your first conversation with [Wedded Concierge]" New: "Bring this list to every venue visit, and to your first conversation with [Wedded Concierge]"

suggested_edits.old: A garden is the loveliest setting to get right and the easiest to leave to chance.
suggested_edits.new: A garden has more to settle in advance than an indoor room, and more that can change on the day.
suggested_edits.why: Removes emotional language and a scare line; keeps the same meaning in plain terms. Adds no facts.

suggested_edits.old: the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
suggested_edits.new: the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming, and ask how the fee is worked out before you commit to anything.
suggested_edits.why: Invites the question every sceptical reader has without stating any fee model or business detail.

suggested_edits.old: Bring this list to your first conversation with [Wedded Concierge]
suggested_edits.new: Bring this list to every venue visit, and to your first conversation with [Wedded Concierge]
suggested_edits.why: Makes the checklist feel like help rather than a lead magnet. Adds no facts.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and pricing first, wants proof, fee model and commissions
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions and reviews listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old strings from the draft and add no prices, venue or vendor names, statistics, business details or new facts about real weddings
Scores are 1 to 5 and top_3_changes has at most 3 items

assumptions: Persona is provisional and not CRM-calibrated (evidence_base: assumed), so reactions reflect the card only.
Arrival context not specified by the orchestrator; read as if arriving from a search while comparing planners.
Markdown link syntax is kept in quotes where the sentence contains a link, so quotes match the draft exactly.

open_questions.question: Is there an approved page or sentence describing the Wedded Concierge fee model and supplier commission policy that this post could link to? Without it the sceptic will not enquire from this page.
Do any of the eight linked real wedding stories publish guest numbers, month or wet weather outcomes that could be added from source, to make that section read as proof rather than mood?
